title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: When a Friend Becomes a Caregiver
summary: People outside the family frequently step into helping roles when older adults need assistance.

title: Rural Americans Wait After Judge Delivers Mixed Ruling on Digital Equity Dollars
summary: A federal judge ruled that President Donald Trump can’t unilaterally kill the $2.75 billion Digital Equity Act, but he also sided with the administration by saying using race as a factor in awarding the grants is unconstitutional. The split decision has halted digital-skills programs for ethnic and racial minorities.

title: A NY Hospital Tried To Close Its Birthing Center. This City United To Fight Back.
summary: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, New York, joined together to challenge a national Catholic health system determined to close the last birthing center in the county.

title: Nonprofits Are Helping Musicians Pay for Insurance in Austin, Texas, and Beyond
summary: A nonprofit and a local public health agency are subsidizing marketplace health insurance for Austin music artists, even as shifting marketplace conditions make the program a more expensive proposition. It’s becoming a model for other cities and sectors.

title: Democrats Demand Trump Administration Halt Collection of Patients’ ER Records
summary: Senate and House Democrats say the Trump administration’s plan to collect patients’ medical data violates privacy and will discourage people from seeking medical care.

title: The Market Forces Quietly Adding Thousands to Patient Bills
summary: The true cost of “vertical integration”: patients directed to a higher-priced location for procedures. Or forced to buy from their insurer’s wholly owned pharmacy, which may not stock the drug prescribed or provide it at the lowest price.

title: ‘It’s Triage’: California’s Next Governor Will Face Destabilizing Surge in Uninsured
summary: The nation’s uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California’s next governor as states stare down the biggest rise in the uninsured rate in a generation.

title: With Midterms Looming, Journalists Consider Measles, Food Recalls, and Obamacare
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: Trump and Kennedy’s Health Industry Deals Haven’t Been Enforced and Are at Risk of Vanishing
summary: The agreements, covering issues like drug pricing, reducing the use of synthetic food dyes, and cutting back on insurance prior authorization rules, were announced with fanfare and touted as victories. But it’s not clear whether they’ll result in lasting change.
